observation.visible_scene: A wooded clearing in late autumn/winter. A large, dark tree stump stands center-frame; its left and front faces are engulfed in bright orange-yellow flames, while its right side is blackened and mostly unburned. A pile of weathered fallen logs and bare branches lies around the stump's base, with a small secondary flame flickering on one log in the foreground. The ground is covered in dry leaves and patchy grass; tall bare and pine trees fill the background, with a fence and open field visible at the far left.
visible_changes: The main fire on the stump's left face burns continuously throughout, its shape and height flickering and reshaping frame to frame without extinguishing.
Intermittent flame tongues and glowing embers rise above the top edge of the stump (notably a tall plume around t=2.27–2.40 s and smaller ember spots earlier), then subside.
The small flame on the foreground log flickers in size, sometimes growing into a short vertical tongue, sometimes shrinking to a point.

The framing drifts slowly: the stump and logs shift progressively toward the right side of the frame while more of the left background (fence, road, field) is revealed, indicating a slow leftward camera pan/truck rather than movement of the stump or logs themselves.
The stump, log pile, and background trees remain fixed in position relative to the ground; only the flames and embers move as objects.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and when the fire was ignited, and whether it is growing or decaying overall (the excerpt shows only steady ongoing burning).
What occurs after the last frame or before the first frame.
Whether any person or tool is involved (none is visible).
uncertain_details: The exact magnitude and type of camera motion (pan vs. lateral track) is inferred only from the consistent rightward shift of the static scene and the leftward reveal of background; no parallax cue confirms distance.
Whether the rising embers/flame tongues are sparks carried by wind or part of the stump's own combustion cannot be determined from the frames.
